findings.title: Chunk footer after chunk data is not validated to be CRLF (request smuggling primitive)
findings.evidence:
CVE-2025-43859: ChunkedReader consumes exactly self._bytes_to_discard (=2, a bare count set at h11/_readers.py:197) bytes after each chunk and accepts them unconditionally. At lines 163-167 it calls buf.maybe_extract_at_most(self._bytes_to_discard) and only subtracts len(data); it never compares the bytes to b'
' as RFC 7230 requires, so ANY two bytes terminate a chunk. The upstream fix (0.16.0) changed _bytes_to_discard to b'
' and raises LocalProtocolError('malformed chunk footer') on mismatch. The bytes are fully attacker-controlled and reach the sink directly: ChunkedReader is the body reader selected by the attacker's 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' header (READERS map, h11/_readers.py:243), fed from the raw connection by Connection.receive_data. Verified against this exact 0.14.0 tree: h11.Connection(CLIENT).receive_data(b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

5
HELLOXX0

') yields Response, Data(b'HELLO'), EndOfMessage (the junk 'XX' footer is accepted), and any bytes following it are parsed as a brand-new message; the pristine 0.16.0 rejects the same stream. A stream that h11 splits at the fake boundary while a stricter intermediary (e.g. a proxy that consumes the chunk terminator with a generic read-until-EOL helper) splits it differently is the classic front-end/back-end desync, enabling HTTP request smuggling and request/response queue poisoning. Per the advisory, standalone exploitation requires a co-located parser whose chunk parsing diverges, so this is a smuggling primitive reachable whenever h11 parses untrusted chunked framing rather than an end-to-end exploit by itself.
